project.name: relaydesk-telegram-support
project.description: RelayDesk turns a single Telegram Business account into a shared team inbox where support staff work through individual web identities without sharing Telegram credentials or sessions. It provides webhook-driven conversations, assignment, status and priority workflows, folder routing, media handling, D1 persistence, allowed-email authentication, and webhook-secret validation.

tour.title: RelayDesk Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand how RelayDesk turns one Telegram Business account into a shared support inbox. It connects the hosted webhook path, the optional local Telegram tooling, D1 persistence, and operator configuration into one deployment story. This context provides the vocabulary for every later stop in the tour.

tour.title: Inbox Entry Point
tour.description: The Next.js home route mounts the support desk, which is the central client coordinator for authentication, polling, filtering, messages, replies, assignment, and administrative tools. Shared view types define the actors, conversations, messages, folders, and status data exchanged with the server. Together these files reveal the user-facing shape of the system before the tour follows its network calls inward.
tour.languageLesson: React client coordinators commonly use hooks to keep remote state and UI state synchronized, while TypeScript interfaces make the data exchanged between components and route handlers explicit.

tour.title: Team Authentication
tour.description: Before the inbox from Step 2 can load, RelayDesk resolves a support actor through first-run setup or password login. The account UI exposes that flow, while the route handlers and shared authentication modules enforce roles, persist sessions, construct secure cookies, and hash credentials and tokens. This boundary protects both ordinary agent work and administrator-only team management.
tour.languageLesson: Web Crypto keeps password and session-token handling on standards-based primitives; the server stores one-way hashes and gives the browser a secure session cookie rather than exposing reusable credentials.

tour.title: Inbox Read Flow
tour.description: Once authenticated, the support desk reads operational state through the conversation, message, and status endpoints. These handlers collapse duplicate topic roots, return chronological messages, clear unread counts, update assignment or status with auditing, and report Telegram and listener health. This is the read-and-control path that keeps the shared inbox responsive to multiple agents.

tour.title: Telegram Message Intake
tour.description: The webhook route is the hosted ingestion boundary for Telegram Business, group, channel, edited, and deleted message events. It verifies the shared secret and deduplicates updates before the Telegram adapter normalizes payloads and the storage service updates conversations, messages, unread state, previews, and deletion markers. This pipeline supplies the live data displayed by the read endpoints from Step 4.

tour.title: Replies and Auditing
tour.description: Agent actions travel back to Telegram through separate text and media reply routes. Shared validation ensures the destination and any referenced message belong to the selected conversation, while outbound content is persisted and added to a retention-managed audit log. The administrator message-log panel then turns that audit trail into a searchable, paginated operational view.

tour.title: Folders and Listeners
tour.description: RelayDesk extends the basic inbox with Telegram folder-driven routing and account-side synchronization. Signed folder snapshots map peers to agents and recalculate conversation ownership, while listener heartbeats and authenticated history imports expose the health and backfill channels used by local MTProto tools. The folder rules panel gives administrators a visual control surface for this automatic assignment layer.

tour.title: D1 Data Layer
tour.description: All API and service flows converge on a typed Drizzle entry point for the Cloudflare D1 binding. The schema defines agents, sessions, Telegram connections and folders, conversations, messages, webhook deduplication, audits, and retained logs, while runtime initialization applies compatibility upgrades and cleanup idempotently. Drizzle configuration links this TypeScript model to the generated SQLite migrations explored next.

tour.title: Schema Evolution
tour.description: The initial migration establishes the core inbox tables, and the latest migration adds Telegram folder membership plus assignment provenance to conversations. Drizzle's journal preserves the ordered six-revision history, while hosting configuration binds the deployed application to its D1 database. These artifacts show how the data model from Step 8 evolves safely and becomes available at runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Ordered SQL migrations record incremental schema changes, while generated snapshots and a migration journal let tooling compare the expected model with deployed SQLite state.

tour.title: Local Setup Bridge
tour.description: For local development, the six-step setup wizard delegates privileged machine operations to an authenticated loopback-only Python bridge. The PowerShell orchestrator prepares secrets and launches the bridge, web server, optional user listener, and bot poller, while the session helper protects persistent Telegram credentials with Windows DPAPI. This design keeps machine-specific authorization outside the browser process while preserving an approachable setup experience.
tour.languageLesson: A loopback bridge can safely expose narrowly scoped native capabilities to a local web UI when requests are authenticated and the service is not bound to external interfaces; DPAPI ties encrypted session material to the current Windows account.

tour.title: Telegram Local Relays
tour.description: The local integration path offers complementary transports for bringing Telegram activity into the same APIs used by production. Bot API long polling securely relays supported updates to the webhook, the persistent MTProto listener backfills and streams groups, channels, topics, folders, and heartbeats, and the one-time importer synchronizes bounded history batches. The pinned Python requirements make those Telethon-based tools reproducible for operators.

tour.title: Runtime and Build
tour.description: The Cloudflare Worker is the production entry point, routing application requests and delegating image and static-asset work to platform bindings. Vite and Vinext adapt the Next-compatible application for local emulation and Cloudflare deployment, while the package manifest and strict TypeScript configuration define the build commands, dependencies, runtime version, and path aliases. These files explain how the UI and API layers become one deployable edge application.

tour.title: Build Contract Test
tour.description: Finish with the rendered-HTML smoke test, which verifies that the built server bundle exists and checks key application, API, listener, feature, and security contracts. It acts as a compact cross-layer safety net for the architecture visited throughout the tour. Reading it last shows which RelayDesk behaviors the project treats as essential release invariants.
tour.languageLesson: A smoke test favors broad, fast contract checks over exhaustive behavior coverage, making it useful as a final build gate while narrower tests handle detailed logic.
